summary: Karen Nelson Villanueva is a religious studies scholar who earned her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2013). She also studied under traditional teachers Geshe Ngawang Dakpa and Lobsang Chökyi (attested 2013).
Karen Nero held academic posts at the University of Canterbury from around 1998 to 2006 and at the University of Otago around 2007.

Karen O'Brien-Kop is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London, where she was a senior teaching fellow, and later became lecturer in Asian Religions and Ethics at University of Roehampton.

Karin Meyers is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Jay L. Garfield. She served at Kathmandu University as an assistant professor and director of the Buddhist studies MA program at the Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Karin Preisendanz is an Indologist and philosopher who earned her Dr. phil. and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She held positions at the Free University of Berlin, the University of British Columbia, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Vienna.

Karl Ammer (1911–1970) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Vienna. From circa 1955 to 1970, he held a post at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and directed the Institute of Indology at the University of Halle.

Karl Benedikt Hase (1780–1864) was a linguist and historian. After studying at the universities of Jena and Helmstedt, he held long-term posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, the École des Langues Orientales, and the Faculty of Arts of Paris.

Karl Brugmann (1849–1919) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Halle and Leipzig, completing his doctorate under Georg Curtius. He held professorships at the University of Freiburg and the University of Leipzig, where he taught until 1919.

Karl Brunnhölzl is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Khenpo Lama Thubten.

Karl Debreczeny is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Wu Hung and teacher Jenny Purtle, and later served as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2008).

Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal (1812–1894) was a historian. He studied at Sächsisches Landesgymnasium Sankt Afra zu Meißen and the universities of Leipzig, Berlin, and Heidelberg, later holding a post at the University of Heidelberg from around 1842 to 1845.

Karl Eugen Neumann (1865–1915) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig from around 1887 to 1888 and completed his doctorate under Richard Pischel around 1888 to 1891.
Karl Felix Halm (1809–1882) was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. From circa 1856 to 1882, he held posts at the University of Munich and the Bavarian State Library.
Karl Ferdinand Johansson (1860–1926) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Uppsala University beginning in 1880 and later served there as a professor from circa 1893 to 1925.

Karl Florenz (1865–1939) was a scholar of Japanology, linguistics, and religion. He studied at Leipzig and Berlin, taught German literature at the University of Tokyo (1889–1917), and held chairs at the Hamburg Colonial Institute and the University of Hamburg.

Karl Friedrich Geldner (1852–1929) was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar. He studied at Leipzig and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and held positions at Tübingen, Halle, Berlin, and the University of Marburg, where he was Sanskrit professor from 1907 to 1921.
Karl G. Heider is an academic who completed studies at Williams College (~1952–1954), Harvard College (~1954–1956), and Harvard University (~1956–1966).

Karl H. Potter (1927–2022) was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at California and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, held professorships at the universities of Minnesota and Washington, and served as General Editor of the Encyclopedia of Indian Philosophies.

Karl Hoffmann (1915–1996) was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranianist. He studied at Munich under Ferdinand Sommer and Walther Wüst, later holding chairs in Indo-European and Indo-Iranian studies at Saarland University (1952–1955) and FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg (1955–1983).

Karl Jettmar (1918–2002) was an archaeologist, Indologist, and Iranian studies scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna. He held positions at Weltmuseum Wien, the Frobenius Institute, and the universities of Vienna, Mainz, and Heidelberg.
